The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

forecasts.rationale: The Fed hiked a quarter point to 3.75-4.00% on Sept 16 (unanimous). The Oct 7 minutes say most officials see another hike as likely by year end, but Jefferson and Williams signalled patience, and CME FedWatch (futures, not a betting market) showed about 80% pricing a hold for Oct 27-28. December is the more likely hike meeting, with a new SEP.

Base rate: In a tightening cycle the Fed often hikes at consecutive meetings, but pauses are common when data is mixed. Evidence: Fed funds futures price an 80% chance of a hold at the October 27-28 meeting, while the October 7 minutes show most officials expect another hike by year-end, pointing to a possible December move instead. This probability could shift if upcoming inflation or employment data materially alters expectations before the meeting.

Historically, the Fed holds rates about 30% of the time at any given meeting (base rate). After the September 25‑bp hike, minutes showed most officials favor another hike, but Fed funds futures priced an 80% chance of a hold at the October meeting, reflecting market expectations. This shifts the probability toward a hold, though unexpected inflation or labor data could prompt a hike, lowering the chance.

The base rate for no change is around 50%, but the evidence strongly favors a hold. The FOMC hiked in September, and minutes indicate most expect another hike by year-end, but not necessarily in October. Fed funds futures price an 80% chance of a hold, and some officials suggest waiting for more data. This supports a high probability of no change at the October meeting.

Fed funds futures price roughly an 80% chance of a hold at the October meeting, providing a strong base rate. While the September minutes revealed 16 of 18 officials project at least one more 2026 hike, influential policymakers Vice Chair Jefferson and NY Fed President Williams advocated waiting for more data, tilting the balance toward a pause in October. Unexpectedly strong inflation or labor-market reports before the October 27–28 meeting could still prompt the Committee to hike earlier than futures currently imply.

The base rate for a given FOMC meeting is usually a hold, but the September 2026 hike and hawkish dot projections make a change more plausible than in a normal cycle. The strongest specific evidence is that Fed funds futures priced about an 80% chance of a hold for October, with the remaining hike likely deferred to December. Incoming inflation or labor data, or a more hawkish statement, could push the probability lower.

Base rate for FOMC holds at any given meeting is roughly 60-70% historically, but recent evidence strongly favors a hold: the Sept 16 hike was unanimous, minutes show most officials expect only one more hike by year-end (likely December, which carries new projections), and FedWatch prices ~80% chance of a hold at the Oct 27-28 meeting. The October meeting is a non-Sep/Dec meeting without new SEP projections, making a hold more likely as the Fed saves action for December. A surprise hike remains possible given inflation persistence, but the evidence tilts clearly toward no change.

This market will resolve according to the change in basis points in the deposit facility rate resulting from the October 2026 meeting of the European Central Bank, relative to the level it was prior to this meeting.

The resolution source will be official information from the European Central Bank, including the statement or release from its October 2026 meeting, scheduled for October 28-29, 2026, as listed on the official European Central Bank calendar (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/mgcgc/html/index.en.html). This market may resolve as soon as the statement or release of the European Central Bank's October 2026 meeting with relevant data is issued.

If the specified rate is defined by an upper and lower bound, the relevant change will be the change to the upper bound.

If the specified rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded according to the following guidelines. Increases or decreases of less than 25 bps will be rounded to 25 bps (e.g. an increase or decrease of 10 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 25 bps). Increases or decreases of greater than 25 bps will be rounded to the nearest 25 bps and will be rounded away from 0 in cases of equidistance (e.g., an increase or decrease of 37.5 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 50 bps). Displayed options of “Increase” or “Decrease” will include policy rate increases or decreases of any size.

If the specified meeting is postponed to a date and time before the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve based on the outcome of that postponed meeting. If the specified meeting is cancelled, or postponed such that no decision is announced by the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the “No Change” bracket. Emergency changes to the specified rate not resulting from the specified meeting will not be considered.

forecasts.rationale: The ECB raised the deposit rate to 2.50% on Sept 10. Lagarde struck a dovish tone in early October, arguing higher long-term yields will slow growth and dampen energy pass-through; Ebury (Oct 8) sees an October hike as unlikely despite a September inflation beat, with December still live. Rates futures had about a 60% chance of an October hike on Sept 24, so a hike stays a real risk.

Base rate for ECB meetings is roughly a 60% chance of no change given recent tightening cycles, but the September 25bp hike and hawkish comments shift odds toward another increase. Market futures priced a 60% chance of an October hike, while analyst views are split (Danske expects a hike, Goldman/UBS see December, MUFG sees no further hikes), implying about a one‑third chance of an October hike from that perspective. Averaging the market and analyst signals yields ~46‑47% probability of a hike, so the probability of no change is about 55%.

The base rate for no change at a meeting following a recent hike is moderate, but Lagarde's unexpectedly dovish early-October comments, emphasizing that rising long-term yields will slow growth and damp inflation pass-through, significantly reduce the likelihood of a hike. Ebury's judgment that an October hike is unlikely and the shift from prior futures pricing (60% hike probability before the dovish tone) support a higher chance of no change, though lingering hawkish risks from September's inflation beat and Nagel's cautious stance prevent a higher probability.

The base rate favors a pause after a September hike, and Lagarde's early-October dovish pivot—arguing that higher long-term yields will slow growth and dampen energy pass-through—combined with Ebury's assessment that an October hike is unlikely, strongly point to no change. While futures had priced a significant chance of a hike as of late September and some analysts still expect one, the freshest guidance from the ECB President tilts the balance toward steady rates. The main risks to this view are a further upside inflation surprise or an escalation in the Iran war before the meeting.

The base rate for a hold in an active hiking cycle is roughly 50-60%, but the September 25bp hike and inflation beat made another increase plausible. The main evidence shifting the estimate is Lagarde's early-October dovish tone and Ebury's view that an October hike is unlikely, which favors a hold. A surprise energy shock, stronger inflation data, or hawkish ECB officials could still push the market toward a 25bp increase.

Base rate for ECB holding rates steady at any given meeting is roughly 50-60%. The evidence is mixed: futures priced ~60% for a hike in late September, but Lagarde's early October dovish comments and Ebury's assessment that an October hike is unlikely pull toward no change. Goldman, UBS, and MUFG expect no October hike, while Danske expects one. The dovish shift in Lagarde's tone and the tightening of financial conditions via higher long-term yields suggest the ECB will likely pause in October, though a September inflation beat keeps the possibility of a hike alive.

forecasts.rationale: Euro area GDP grew 1.2% year on year in Q2 2026 (third estimate, Sept 7), up from 0.6% in Q1, with a strong 0.6% q/q. Q3 year-on-year growth is roughly the Q2 rate plus Q3 2026 q/q growth minus Q3 2025 q/q growth (about 0.2-0.3%). The energy shock and possible Irish payback point to a weaker Q3, so 0.8-1.0% is about as likely as 1.1% or more (a 1.1% print counts toward the higher bracket). Trading Economics forecasts 1.0%.

The Trading Economics forecast of 1.0% y/y centers in the 0.8-1.1% range, supported by Q2's upward revision to 1.2% y/y and favorable base effects from weak Q3 2025 growth. However, ECB rate hikes in July and September 2026 plus the Iran war energy shock create material downside risk, and the narrow 0.3pp range with three weeks until the flash estimate implies significant uncertainty.

Base rate: historically, Eurozone Q3 YoY GDP growth falls in the 0.8‑1.1% range only about a quarter of the time. Recent evidence shows Q2 2026 YoY growth at +1.2% (up from +0.6% in Q1) and Trading Economics' model forecasts Q3 2026 at +1.0% YoY, suggesting the economy is hovering around the middle of the target band. The ECB's rate hikes and energy‑price shock pose downside risks, while a stronger‑than‑expected rebound from the Iran‑war shock could push growth above 1.1%. Balancing these factors yields a moderate probability that the flash estimate will land between 0.8% and 1.1% (exclusive of 1.1).

The base rate for a narrow GDP growth range is low, but the Trading Economics model forecast of 1.0% y/y for Q3 2026, combined with a low base from Q3 2025, suggests a reasonable chance of the outcome falling in the 0.8-1.0% range (Yes). However, the ECB rate hikes and energy price shock from the Iran war introduce downside risks that could push growth below 0.8% or keep it at 1.0%, making the probability moderately above 50%.

The base rate for Eurozone annual GDP growth landing in any given 0.3 percentage point bracket is roughly 1/3. Recent data shows Q2 2026 at 1.2% y/y (revised up) and Q1 at 0.6% y/y, suggesting momentum but with ECB rate hikes and energy shock weighing on growth. Trading Economics' model forecast of 1.0% y/y for Q3 2026 falls squarely in the 0.8-1.1% bracket, but the wide range of possible outcomes given the energy shock and rate hikes keeps probability below 50%.

forecasts.rationale: The Atlanta Fed GDPNow estimate for Q3 2026 was 3.7% on Oct 6 and 3.6% on Oct 8, down from an initial 5.0% in late September; inventories contribute about 2 points of it, net exports subtract about 2.7 points, and consumption is running at 3.4%. The Philadelphia Fed SPF (Aug 14) was lower at 2.5%. With the advance estimate due Oct 29, GDPNow at this stage has a typical error of about 1.5 points and inventory-heavy readings tend to revise toward consensus, so >3.0% is a bit better than even.

The base rate for quarterly annualized GDP growth exceeding 3% is roughly 40-45%. The Atlanta Fed GDPNow nowcast stands at 3.6% as of October 8, which, given a typical forecast error of about 0.8 percentage points at this horizon, implies a ~75% chance of exceeding 3%. However, the nowcast has fallen steadily from 5.0% in late September, and the large, volatile contributions from inventories (+1.98 points) and investment (+21.5%) increase the risk of downward revisions as more source data arrive. The older SPF median forecast of 2.5% also suggests some downside risk. Balancing these factors yields a probability of about 65%.

Historically, US quarterly real GDP growth exceeds 3% about 35% of the time (base rate). The Atlanta Fed GDPNow estimate for Q3 2026 has been trending downward from 5.0% to 3.6% but remains above the 3.0% threshold, while the Philadelphia Fed Survey of Professional Forecasters projects a lower 2.5% growth. The mixed signals suggest a moderate chance above 3%, leading to an estimated probability of roughly 60%.

The base rate for US GDP growth exceeding 3.0% in any given quarter is low (around 10-15% historically), but the GDPNow tracker consistently estimates Q3 2026 growth well above 3.0%, with latest readings around 3.6%. While the Survey of Professional Forecasters is lower at 2.5%, the GDPNow model has been reasonably accurate historically, and the strength in investment and consumption suggests a significant probability of exceeding 3.0%. However, GDPNow is known to converge toward the advance estimate over time, so further downward revisions before October 29 could lower the probability.

The base rate for a US quarterly GDP print above 3.0% is moderate, but the latest GDPNow of 3.6% is the strongest signal and puts the advance estimate above the threshold. The main uncertainty is that GDPNow can be noisy, especially with large swings in investment, inventories, and net exports, while the Philadelphia Fed survey is lower at 2.5%. A final print would need to fall more than 0.6 points below the current nowcast to resolve No, which is plausible but not likely.

The Atlanta Fed GDPNow estimate, currently at 3.6% (down from an initial 5.0%), is above the 3.0% threshold, providing a positive signal. This market will resolve to “Yes” if a diplomatic agreement between Oman and Iran over traffic in the strait of Hormuz is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

A diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between Oman and Iran.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement must establish Iranian or Omani policies, obligations, or commitments aimed at managing, permitting, restoring, or increasing vessel or shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, including agreements defining vessel traffic corridors, fee collection policies, or other management policies.

All listed countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for the Payout Condition to be met. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.
 
Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where an announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, this market will resolve based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of Oman and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

forecasts.rationale: Iran's foreign ministry said on Oct 7 that Iran and Oman agreed coordinates of safe routes through Hormuz and how to notify the maritime authority (IRNA via Gulf News). The rule needs both countries to announce acceptance of the same agreement. Work is advanced, but Iran ties reopening to US commitments, the IRGC threatens to block the southern route, and the US blockade continues, so a clean joint announcement by Oct 31 is possible but not the base case.

Base rate for diplomatic agreements between regional rivals under active tension with third-party dependencies is low (~15-20% in short windows). Evidence shows only a framework from August with asymmetric announcements (Iran detailing terms, Oman saying 'deal near'), and Iran's Oct 7 statement describes technical coordination on coordinates, not formal acceptance of a binding agreement. Major blockers remain: Iran conditions Hormuz access on US commitments and IRGC control, an IRGC adviser threatened to block the southern route, and the US port blockade continues. Talks on permanent terms, fees, and traffic management are explicitly 'still to come.' With 19 days left and no Omani confirmation since August, the probability of both countries formally announcing acceptance of the same qualifying agreement by Oct 31 is low. Could increase if US-Iran talks progress or Oman issues a clear acceptance statement.

The base rate for a bilateral Hormuz traffic agreement between Oman and Iran being announced in any given month is low, likely under 10%. Iran's Oct 7 statement indicates progress on a temporary corridor, but Oman has not yet announced acceptance, and the IRGC adviser's threat signals internal Iranian obstacles. With unresolved issues and only 19 days remaining, the chance of both countries officially accepting the same agreement by the deadline is modest.

Diplomatic agreements on contested shipping corridors rarely move from a preliminary framework to mutually announced final acceptance in under three weeks. The evidence shows a persistent asymmetry: Iran has unilaterally claimed progress on safe-route coordinates, while Oman has not echoed these specifics and officials explicitly note that talks on fees, permanent arrangements, and traffic management are ongoing. Iran’s insistence that the strait stays closed until U.S. conditions are met—alongside continuing U.S. port blockades and IRGC threats to seal the southern route—makes a bilateral, traffic-restoring announcement by October 31 improbable. The probability would rise sharply only if both capitals suddenly issued a joint statement confirming a finalized text, but the current trajectory points to prolonged negotiation rather than imminent mutual acceptance.

Base rate for a formal bilateral maritime agreement in a high-tension strait within three weeks is low, but the August framework and Iran's October 7 statement that safe-route coordinates were agreed make a limited corridor deal plausible. The key missing piece is an unambiguous Omani acceptance, and the absence of a new Omani statement plus U.S. blockade/IRGC closure warnings lowers the probability. An Omani or joint announcement, or credible reporting confirming Omani acceptance, would push this up sharply.

Base rate for contentious bilateral agreements with unresolved third-party issues in ~19 days is low (~10-15%). Evidence moving probability up is clear momentum: Aug framework deal, Oct 7 Iran announcement on coordinates, and Oman signaling proximity to deal. Evidence moving probability down includes: U.S. commitments under the June memorandum remain unmet (Iran's precondition), ongoing U.S. blockade, IRGC adviser threats against the southern route, no formal matching Omani acceptance announcement, and the fact that talks on permanent arrangement/fees are still pending. A material shift would occur if Oman publicly confirms acceptance of the temporary corridor agreement, or if U.S.-Iran tensions de-escalate.

Resolution Criteria

 * Market Start & Effective Window: This market only evaluates events and price movements occurring on or after the market creation date (September 29, 2026, 21:00 GMT+8 / 13:00 UTC). Prior historical events (including the June 2026 temporary ceasefire and framework agreement) form part of the pre-market background and will not retroactively trigger resolution.

 * Resolves YES if the price of Bitcoin (BTC) reaches or exceeds $105,000.00 USD before the Strait of Hormuz is officially and fully declared "freely open" to standard commercial shipping.

 * Resolves NO if the Strait of Hormuz is officially and fully declared "freely open" before Bitcoin's price reaches $105,000.00 USD.

"Freely Open" Definition (De Jure & De Facto)

The Strait of Hormuz will be considered "freely open" only when both of the following criteria are met:

 * De Jure Official Declarations: Official, formal claims from the governments/military authorities of both the United States and Iran explicitly stating that all blockades, counter-blockades, and closures have officially ended.

 * De Facto Sustained Resumption: Major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg) or maritime authorities (e.g., Lloyd's List) report that security threats have subsided, and normal, unescorted merchant shipping and oil tanker transit volume has returned to sustained pre-war corridor levels.

 * Note: Brief, temporary increases in vessel traffic or temporary ceasefire windows without full bilateral declarations and sustained unescorted transit do not satisfy this condition.

Bitcoin Price Source

Bitcoin's price will be verified using historical or real-time data on CoinGecko or Coinbase. A single verified transaction or price tick at or above $105,000.00 USD on any major, high-volume exchange is sufficient to satisfy the Bitcoin condition.

Market Close Date & Extensions

The close date of this market will be extended periodically as long as neither condition has been met. This market will not resolve to N/A due to time expiration, and will remain active until one of the two outcomes definitively occurs.

Edge Cases

If both events occur on the same calendar day after creation, the exact UTC timestamps of the first official news announcement of the Strait reopening and the $105,000.00 BTC price tick will determine the outcome. If the conflict ends but minor navigation restrictions persist, the market will resolve based on the consensus of maritime shipping reports regarding whether shipping traffic volume has returned to normal peacetime levels.

Background

The Strait of Hormuz has been heavily restricted and effectively closed to normal commercial shipping since late February 2026, following the outbreak of the 2026 U.S.-Iran war and subsequent IRGC naval actions and sea mining. In retaliation, the U.S. implemented a counter-blockade of Iranian ports. As of late September 2026, transit through the strategic choke point remains at a near-total standstill. Concurrently, Bitcoin is trading in the $84,000 to $86,000 range, having previously peaked near $126,000 in late 2025/early 2026 before retracing. This market tracks whether the geopolitical crisis will resolve before Bitcoin re-establishes its upward momentum to break the $105,000 threshold.

forecasts.rationale: BTC traded about $84,050 on Oct 12, so $105,000 needs about +25%; October's high so far is $86,980. The Strait of Hormuz is closed per Iran and contested by the US, there is a US blockade, talks are stalled (Iran called the US response insufficient on Oct 11), and the market's 'freely open' bar requires both governments to declare closures ended plus sustained normal unescorted traffic. Neither condition looks likely by the Oct 31 close, and a quick Hormuz reopening would itself likely lift BTC only modestly. The market says it extends its close date until one side occurs, so a Yes from a long BTC run is possible later.

Base rate: Bitcoin has roughly a 30% chance of achieving a 25% monthly gain based on historical volatility. Evidence: BTC is currently around $84k, needing a 25% rise to $105k, and has only risen ~3.5% in the past week; the Strait of Hormuz remains closed with recent mine strikes and opposing declarations, making a near‑term reopening unlikely. If the Strait stays closed for several weeks, Bitcoin’s chance to reach $105k first approximates its own chance of that price move, yielding a probability below 0.5.

Bitcoin reaching $105,000 from ~$84,050 is a ~25% move, which is within range of recent volatility (peaked at $126,000 in early 2026). The Strait of Hormuz reopening requires both a U.S.–Iran diplomatic breakthrough and sustained normal traffic; current evidence (rejected proposals, recent mine incident) suggests this is not imminent. Given the faster potential for a crypto rally versus a complex geopolitical resolution, Bitcoin touching $105,000 first is moderately more likely.

Base rate for a 25% BTC move before a high-bar geopolitical normalization is roughly even, but the Strait's full reopening requires bilateral declarations and sustained unescorted traffic, and the recent mine and Iran's rejection of the U.S. response make that unlikely soon. BTC is only 25% below $105k and could spike on de-escalation or macro liquidity before de facto shipping normalizes. Weak ETF flows and the war's risk-off effect keep the probability below a strong majority, while a rapid bilateral declaration and traffic normalization would push it lower.

Base rate for an unknown geopolitical-crypto race: roughly even but with crypto moves often faster. Evidence pushing down: BTC needs ~25% to reach $105k from ~$84k in under 20 days with no clear catalyst, while a mine strike on Oct 10-11 and Iran's rejection of the U.S. proposal on Oct 11 suggest the Strait remains far from 'freely open' under the strict bilateral/sustained-traffic definition. However, the requirement for BOTH de jure declarations and de facto sustained unescorted traffic is a high bar that makes early Strait reopening unlikely, which could push toward YES. A surprise diplomatic deal could flip this quickly.

Products labeled as a GA promotion of an already-existing Preview model (e.g., gemini-3.1-pro-ga) may qualify.

A qualifying model must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must either be clearly defined and publicly announced by Google as accessible to the general public, or otherwise be made publicly accessible and explicitly labeled on the company's official website. Labeling errors, placeholder text, or version names displayed on the website that do not correspond to a model that is actually accessible to the general public will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Google, with additional verification from a consensus of credible reporting.

I discount for the strict rule that Saudi forces themselves must have conducted the strike (not the coalition or Yemeni forces), the heavy reliance on Houthi-run sources for attribution, a possible ceasefire before Oct 30 and the absence of reporting I found after about Oct 19.

The Saudi-backed offensive 'Dawn of Yemen' began Oct 3-4 with intense air operations (324 targets claimed at launch, ~300 strikes/week per Houthi claims) and strikes were reported through Oct 18, suggesting a high base rate of near-daily activity. However, the last specific reporting is from Oct 18 (5 days ago), attribution to Saudi armed forces (vs. coalition/proxy) is often unclear in sources, and a ceasefire or pause before Oct 30 would halt strikes. The 7-day horizon and ongoing offensive favor Yes, but attribution and reporting gaps create significant uncertainty.

The Saudi-led coalition has been conducting near-daily airstrikes since early September 2026 as part of Operation Dawn of Yemen, with direct Saudi involvement reported. Given the intensity and sustained nature of the campaign, a qualifying strike on October 30 is highly likely, but a small chance of a pause, ceasefire, or day without attributable strikes reduces certainty slightly.

The Saudi-led coalition has conducted near-daily air strikes since early September, and Saudi warplanes were explicitly identified in attacks through mid-October during the ongoing Operation Dawn of Yemen; however, no reports were found after about Oct 19, creating uncertainty about whether tempo will persist and whether any Oct 30 strike will be clearly attributed to Saudi armed forces rather than coalition partners. A confirmed ceasefire or pause before Oct 30 would push the probability toward zero, while renewed credible reporting of Saudi-conducted strikes in the immediate days before Oct 30 would raise it.

The base rate is elevated because the evidence describes an ongoing Saudi-led air campaign in Yemen through at least mid-October, with coalition-confirmed strikes and Houthi claims of frequent Saudi aircraft operations. Reports of Saudi F-15/Typhoon strikes from Saudi bases and coalition statements about 100 jets support the possibility of direct Saudi armed-force action, which is the key qualifying condition. I discounted the probability because attribution is often to the broader coalition, Houthi-run sources may overstate or misattribute strikes, and there is no confirmed reporting after about Oct 19, leaving open the chance of a pause, ceasefire, or non-qualifying action on Oct 30.

The base rate is favorable: Saudi aircraft reportedly carried out near-daily strikes during the September–October campaign, and CNN/CBS reporting and a Saudi coalition spokesman’s statement that 100 fighter jets participated support direct Saudi involvement. However, no reporting was found after about October 19, and some incidents are described only as Saudi-led coalition strikes, leaving meaningful uncertainty about a pause, a Yemeni-only operation, or clear attribution on October 30. The probability is therefore about two-thirds; confirmed continued Saudi strikes would raise it, while a ceasefire or shift to Yemeni-only strikes would lower it.

Negative months are rare historically (about 1 in 39), but the trend has turned sharply and two trackers point negative, so I lean slightly to Yes; the sign depends on a few late-month moves and on Black Bird's own method, and the question resolves N/A if it does not publish.

Base rate shows Black Bird reported Russian net gains in ~38 of 39 months from mid-2023 through August 2026, but September broke this pattern with -190 km². Multiple trackers (ISW, Russia Matters) show Russian gains collapsing to near-zero or negative in early October, suggesting a genuine momentum shift. However, the month is not over (today Oct 23), DeepState reports localized Russian advances in the last few days, and the final Black Bird figure could be revised or delayed, creating meaningful uncertainty around the sign of the October net change.

The base rate of negative net Russian monthly advances is very low (about 1 in 39 months since mid-2023), but September 2026 saw a sharp reversal with -190 km². Current October data from various trackers shows near-zero net change, with some sources indicating small Russian gains and others Ukrainian gains. Given the reported Ukrainian initiative and momentum, a negative October figure is more likely than not, but the month is not over and small territorial shifts could easily flip the sign, so confidence is moderate.

Black Bird’s data shows Russian net territorial gains in roughly 38 of the last 39 months, giving a strong base rate for a positive (NO) reading. However, September 2026 broke that streak with a large -190 km² net loss for Russia, and while some trackers suggest Ukraine continued to gain ground in early October, DeepState data through October 19 shows a near-zero net of +3 square miles for Russia, with small Russian advances reported in the final week. With only about eight days left in the month and the net balance effectively at the threshold, minor territorial shifts or the confirmation of disputed claims could easily flip the sign either way.

Black Bird's monthly figure was positive in nearly every month from mid-2023 through August 2026, so the historical base rate for a negative (Yes) result was only about 1 in 39. September's unusual -190 km² result, ISW's reported net Russian loss since September 1, and evidence of sharply shrinking Russian gains raise the odds substantially, although DeepState's slight net Russian gain and continuing local Russian advances keep October close to even. This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Israeli national government, or an authorized representative of the Israeli national government, publicly announces that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused this incident, by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A public announcement refers to an on-the-record statement issued by the Israeli national government or by its authorized representatives acting in an official capacity on behalf of the Israeli national government. A statement or press release issued by the Israeli national government or any of its agencies will qualify. A Prime Minister or Cabinet Minister’s public statements will always be considered to be issued on-the-record in a capacity representing the Israeli national government for purposes of this market. A statement from a lawmaker or other government official speaking in their own capacity or on behalf of a party not in government will not alone qualify.

For purposes of this market, an affiliated group of Iran is: any organization directly controlled by Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, Houthis ("Ansar Allah"), Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Badr Organization, and Harakat al-Nujaba. An unlisted group will only qualify if the Israeli claim itself, or accompanying statements or releases, specifies that the group is a proxy of or otherwise is controlled or directed by Iran. A general statement that it was conducted by an Iranian proxy will also qualify, even if no group is named.

Such a statement will be considered to claim that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused the incident if it explicitly claims that Iran or an affiliated group ordered, carried out, planned, or otherwise directly aided or coordinated the incident. Statements that attribute only inspiration or ideological influence (e.g., "this would not have happened if Iran didn't radicalize terrorists," "the co-pilot was influenced by Hamas' ideas") will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement has been made, no subsequent walkback or retraction will be relevant for purposes of this market. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Israeli national government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

forecasts.rationale: Flydubai FZ1073 was diverted on Sept 30. The co-pilot was reported as an Omani national barred from flying in Oman over extremist views. Israeli investigators told CBS (Oct 4) they believe he was likely a lone wolf, and Netanyahu said it 'looks like a suicide attempt' by someone Islamist-radicalized, not naming Iran. Trump said the co-pilot may be linked to Iran, but Israel has made no such accusation. A UAE official said the co-pilot planned an attack on Ben-Gurion airport. An official Israeli government attribution to Iran or its proxies by Oct 31 would need new evidence.

The base rate for Israel formally accusing Iran or its proxies of a specific aviation incident is low. Current evidence strongly indicates a lone actor: Israeli investigators assess a single actor, Netanyahu calls it a suicide attempt by an Islamist-radicalized individual without naming Iran, and the co-pilot is an Omani national previously barred by Oman for extremist views. The UAE leads the investigation and has not implicated Iran. With only ~19 days until the deadline and no Israeli statement pointing to Iranian direction, the probability remains low but non-zero should new intelligence emerge.

Current evidence points to a lone, Islamist‑radicalized co‑pilot acting alone, with Israeli officials describing it as a suicide attempt and not naming Iran. The explicit statement required by the market—that Iran or an affiliated group deliberately caused the incident—has not been made, and with the investigation led by the UAE and only 19 days remaining, a sudden reversal appears unlikely unless unexpected direct evidence emerges.

Israeli investigators have characterized the attack as a likely lone-wolf incident, and Netanyahu has explicitly described the co-pilot as Islamist-radicalized without naming Iran or any proxy. With 19 days remaining, the trajectory of Israeli rhetoric is moving away from blaming Iran rather than toward it. I assign a low probability, reserving some chance for unexpected evidence or escalation causing Israel to formally accuse Iran.

On October 9, 2026, Donald Trump announced an agreement with Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel fuel, and the United States Treasury issued General License 135 authorizing the importation of Russian-origin diesel fuel into the United States through April 7, 2027 (see: https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117412435306815143 & https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261009_33).

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Russian diesel fuel is imported to the United States between market creation and October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Russian diesel fuel refers to diesel fuel of Russian production origin.

Imported to the United States refers to the diesel fuel being physically delivered to a United States port or into the terrestrial territory of the United States for commercial or government use within the United States. Diesel fuel carried as a vessel’s own fuel, held in bond for re-export, or passing through the United States in transit to another country will not qualify.

To qualify, the import must either be described by a consensus of credible reporting as having been made under the agreement announced on October 9, 2026 (or any amended or successor arrangement between the governments of the United States and Russia), or be authorized under General License 135 (or any amended or successor authorization permitting the importation of Russian-origin diesel fuel).

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

forecasts.rationale: OFAC General License 135 (Oct 9) authorizes Russian-origin diesel imports into the US through April 7, 2027, covering cargoes loaded on tankers as of Oct 9, and Russia partially lifted its diesel export ban on Oct 10 (500,000 tons). Vessel-tracking reports (Vortexa, Windward, VesselFinder, via NV and UNN, Oct 10-11) show the Greek tanker MINERVA ZEN, which left St. Petersburg Sept 22 with about 280,000 barrels of diesel/gasoil, arriving at the US East Coast (Wilmington, NC) around Oct 11-13, which would be a Russian-origin import authorized under the license well before Oct 31. Risks: the single-cargo evidence is OSINT-based, the cargo may be gasoil or discharged elsewhere, and resolution needs consensus credible reporting.

Base rate for US imports of Russian diesel is near zero due to sanctions, but the October 9 General License 135 and Russia's partial export ban lift create a new pathway. A specific tanker (MINERVA ZEN) carrying ~280,000 barrels of Russian diesel is reported en route to Wilmington, NC with an ETA of October 11-13, which would allow physical delivery before the October 31 deadline. However, the vessel-tracking reports are OSINT-only and unconfirmed; EU/UK sanctions and the $100/bbl price cap pose significant compliance hurdles for the Greek-flagged vessel; Russian output is down ~30%; and US political opposition could prompt license reversal. Confirmation of actual offloading would raise probability sharply, while diversion or legal challenges would lower it.

These factors strongly increase the likelihood of an import before the October 31 cutoff. However, potential obstacles such as EU/UK sanctions, the $100 price cap, reduced Russian output, and political opposition could delay or block the shipment, keeping the probability short of certainty.

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Against that, three unconfirmed reports (testingcatalog 17 October, orcarouter 19 October, sandbase 20 October) describe a Fable 5.5 string on Azure, partner checkpoints from 18 October and an expectation of a launch 'next week'; the Azure entry was removed and Anthropic has confirmed nothing, and partner access would not count. I put a public release in the next ten days at about one in three.

Base rate: two Fable releases in 2026 spaced ~84 days apart (Jun 9 and Sep 1), with 50 days since the last. Official Anthropic channels (Fable page, models overview, release notes, newsroom) list only Fable 5.1 as current and show no announcement of a 5.2+ model. Third-party leaks describe partner-only checkpoints and a removed Azure catalog row, but no public model ID, rate card, or general availability. With only 10 days remaining and no official pre-announcement, a public launch by Oct 31 is unlikely.

The base rate of Fable releases (84 days apart) suggests the next one would be due around late November, making a release by October 31 unlikely. However, the rapid cadence of the Claude 5.5 family (three models in 15 days) and unverified leaks about Fable 5.5 increase the chance of an imminent launch, but the leaks' predicted date (October 20) passed without an official announcement, and only 10 days remain. Without a confirmed public model ID or announcement, a release by the deadline is less likely than not.

Base rate from 2026 Fable releases shows an ~84-day gap between general-availability versions, and only 50 days have passed since Fable 5.1, making a late-October release earlier than the established cadence. Unverified leaks about partner checkpoints and a since-removed Azure catalog entry raise a small possibility of a surprise launch, but Anthropic has issued no official announcement and no public model ID is currently callable. With just ten days remaining, the absence of any confirmed public-access signal means a release by October 31 is unlikely.

The base Fable cadence in 2026 (84 days between Fable 5 and 5.1, with 50 days already elapsed) favors no qualifying release in the remaining 10 days, but unconfirmed Fable 5.5 leaks and partner checkpoints raise the chance of a late public launch. As of October 21, Anthropic's official Fable page, models overview, release notes, and newsroom still show only Fable 5.1, and the rumored October 20 date has passed without a public model ID, rate card, or accessible endpoint. An official public announcement or callable public model ID before October 31 would flip the answer, so I assign about 70% to no qualifying release.

Base rate: Anthropic ships models rapidly (5.5 family: Opus 9/22, Sonnet 9/28, Haiku 10/7), and multiple leaks (Azure catalog row, partner checkpoints, social media predictions) suggest Fable 5.5 is imminent. However, the predicted Tuesday launch date (October 20) already passed without an official release, only 10 days remain, and as of October 21 no qualifying model is accessible publicly. The question resolves to Yes if no release happens by Oct 31, so I'm assigning roughly 45% probability to 'no release' reflecting genuine uncertainty between imminent launch versus a delay beyond the resolution date.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the intersection at 48.450545° N, 37.181493° E in Novyi Donbas, Donetsk Oblast, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

The intersection will be considered captured if any part of the intersection is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date.

Any continuous shading under the following layers will qualify:
- Assessed Russian-Controlled Terrain
- Assessed Russian Advances

Shading under the following layers will not qualify:
- Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas
- Claimed Russian Territory

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded under a qualifying layer on the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

Intersection Location in Novyi Donbas: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/Novyi+Donbas1.png

Novyi Donbas Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/Novyi+Donbas2.png

Location on Google Maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/fsRaQXJ6vikXNKYu9

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

forecasts.rationale: ISW's 20 October assessment coded only an infiltration flag-raising at the Almazna mine in the Dobropillya area, a layer that does not qualify, and on 17 October ISW had seen no evidence of Russian consolidation there. DeepState's 13 and 20 October updates say Russian forces advanced 'near' Novyi Donbas without saying the settlement or the intersection is held. Earlier episodes (the failed December 2025 attempt, the 26 January 2026 infiltration that changed no control, and Ukrainian forces present west and south of the village on 28 to 29 August) did not become assessed Russian control, and shading must also persist a full update cycle, so Yes within ten days is unlikely.

Base rate is low given the historical pattern of failed Russian consolidation attempts at Novyi Donbas (Dec 2025, Jan 2026) and current ISW assessments showing only infiltration missions, not assessed control. DeepState reports partial advances near Novyi Donbas but not capture, and ISW daily texts Oct 14-20 do not mention Novyi Donbas. The 10-day window is short for a confirmed map change persisting through an ISW update cycle. Probability could increase if ISW map shading shifts to a qualifying layer at the intersection or a negotiated handover establishes actual control.

The base rate for capturing a specific settlement in a 10-day window is low, and historical Russian attempts at Novyi Donbas have failed to consolidate control. Recent DeepState reports indicate only partial advances, not captures, and ISW's October 20 assessment did not mention any change at the intersection, suggesting no qualifying shading yet. Given ISW's strict criteria and the short time frame, it is unlikely but not impossible that a sustained advance will be confirmed by the deadline.

The base rate for a specific intersection being assessed as Russian-controlled within ten days is low, especially when ISW has not written up Novyi Donbas and recent reports describe only infiltration or partial advances. DeepState’s Oct. 13 and Oct. 20 notes that Russian forces advanced near Novyi Donbas are the main evidence raising the probability, but they do not establish capture of the exact intersection or qualifying ISW shading. A Yes would require a persistent ISW map change under assessed control/advances, or actual negotiated control, and past failed attempts/infiltrations make that less likely.

Base rate for a small settlement like Novyi Donbas being captured within ~10 days is low, and the historical pattern shows three episodes (Dec 2025, Jan 2026, Sep 2026) where Russian infiltration or attempted seizure failed to translate into assessed control. Recent DeepState reports (13 and 20 Oct) describe only partial advances near Novyi Donbas, not capture, and ISW's 20 Oct assessment only coded an infiltration mission at the Almazna mine in Dobropillya, not control of Novyi Donbas. The intersection would need to be shaded as Russian-controlled or Russian advances (not infiltration) and persist through the next ISW update cycle, which is a higher bar than the recent activity suggests. A negotiated handover with actual control or a sudden ISW reassessment would be needed to push this to Yes.

The 52-week low of $3,886 is undated and not confirmed in October. Probability remains low but non-negligible due to event risk.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

forecasts.rationale: WTI settled near $99.47 on Oct 22 (CNBC, 2026-10-22, from a search summary) and $97.15 on Oct 21, so reaching $115 on the ICE Active Month needs a rise of about 16% in roughly six trading days to Oct 30/31. That is rare even in this war-driven 2026 regime (WTI went from about $70 in June to about $99 now over four months), and the Active Month is a backwardated Dec contract, which makes the target harder than the front-month spot price suggests. The residual comes from jump risk: renewed US strikes on Iran or a Hormuz or Saudi supply shock could spike prices, and the exact October high so far is unknown.

Base rate for a 16% WTI rise in six trading days is extremely low (<1%), but the current war-risk regime with Iran mining the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities, and active US strike planning creates a fat-tailed upside. The main catalyst (US strikes on Iran) is reportedly timed for after the November 3 midterms, limiting October probability, while the backwardated December contract and wide Brent-WTI spread (~$13.5) make a $115 print harder than the front-month quotes suggest. A sudden Hormuz closure or major Saudi outage could spike prices intraday, but with only ~6 sessions left and no such event yet, the chance remains modest.

A roughly 16% rise over the remaining six trading sessions would be rare under ordinary oil volatility, placing the base-rate probability low. The Iran/Hormuz and Saudi attacks, shipping disruptions, and possible renewed U.S. strikes materially raise the fat-tail risk. However, the active December WTI contract is near $99.5, so reaching $115 still likely requires a major new supply shock; continued tension without substantial further disruption would probably be insufficient.

An open public preview or beta counts, the way the "DeepSeek-V4 Preview" (April 24) would have. Closed betas, invite-only access, anonymous arena appearances and leaks do not count.

What does NOT count: Flash, Lite, Mini, vision-experimental or distilled models. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash came out on Sept 10, 2026 and does not count, and neither does any later Flash-tier model.

The market resolves NO if any other candidate wins. Resolution will be determined by official results from the Alaska Division of Elections (https://www.elections.alaska.gov/candidates/).

Background

Sullivan, having been re-elected in 2020 with 53.9% of the vote, has declared his re-election bid. Three prominent election forecasters — Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball — currently rate the 2026 Alaska Senate race as "Solid Republican". Sullivan's second-quarter fundraising haul totaled $1.4 million, positioning him well for what appears to be a low-threat election cycle.

Considerations

A jungle primary election will be held on August 18, 2026, from which the top four candidates will advance to the general election. Sullivan has never been in the ranked-choice voting scenario that was implemented in 2022, so this will be his first election in which he faces the "squirrelly voting system that dark-money installed in Alaska" (according to Republicans). Former U.S. Representative from Alaska's at-large congressional district Mary Peltola has also expressed interest in running for this seat; I have a separate market on whether she will run.

forecasts.rationale: Mary Peltola (D) led Sullivan 49.5% to 41.4% in the 18 August primary (Alaska Division of Elections), and Rasmussen's 12 to 15 October poll of 775 likely voters has her ahead 44% to 42%, within the 3-point error. Cook rated the seat a Toss Up on 20 October, and Republican groups have spent more than $18 million (Washington Post, 6 October). Against that, Alaska last elected a Democratic senator in 2008, Sullivan won 53.9% in 2020, and a second Republican named Dan Sullivan on the ballot confuses voters, which the Guardian reported on 14 October. Ranked-choice reallocation is uncertain, so I make Sullivan slightly less than even.

Base rate: Sullivan won 53.9% in 2020 under plurality voting, but this is his first ranked-choice election with a strong Democratic opponent (Peltola) and a same-name Republican spoiler. Evidence: Primary showed Peltola leading by 8 points (49.5% vs 41.4%), but general election polling (Rasmussen, Oct 12-15) shows a statistical tie (Peltola 44%, Sullivan 42%, ±3% MOE). Cook Political Report rates it Toss Up. Structural factors favor Sullivan: incumbent advantage, Alaska's strong Republican lean (Trump won widely in 2024), Trump endorsement, and >$18M in national GOP spending. However, ranked-choice dynamics are unpredictable — second-choice preferences from the two minor Republicans (7% combined) and potential voter confusion between the two Sullivans create significant uncertainty. The race is genuinely competitive; a slight edge to Sullivan reflects the state's partisan baseline and incumbent resources, but Peltola's strength and the novel voting system keep it near a coin flip.

The base rate for an incumbent Republican in Alaska is high, but this race is rated a Toss Up by Cook Political Report and recent polling shows a statistical tie (Peltola 44%, Sullivan 42%). The presence of a second Republican named Dan Sullivan on the ballot introduces significant uncertainty under ranked-choice voting, potentially splitting the GOP vote. However, Alaska's Republican lean, heavy national GOP spending, and Trump's involvement give Sullivan a slight edge, though the outcome is highly uncertain.

The base rate favors an incumbent in a red state, but Sullivan's primary loss and Peltola's lead in the latest Rasmussen poll make this a true toss-up. RCV transfers from the two minor Republican candidates and the six-point undecided pool are the key swing factors, with Trump's endorsement and national GOP spending supporting Sullivan. I put him slightly under even because Peltola's primary and polling lead suggests a modest edge.

Base rate: Alaska is a red-leaning state (Trump won by wide margins, no Dem senator since 2008), and incumbents typically have structural advantages, but the race has shifted dramatically. Evidence: Peltola led the primary 49.5% to 41.4%, Rasmussen shows Peltola 44% to Sullivan 42% with 6% undecided, Cook moved the race to Toss Up, and $18M+ in GOP spending suggests internal concern. The ranked-choice system and the second 'Dan Sullivan' candidate create additional uncertainty that could help Peltola. The race is essentially a toss-up with a slight edge to Peltola given the polling and primary results.

This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

This market will resolve according to the change in basis points in the cash rate target resulting from the November 2026 meeting of the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Monetary Policy Board, relative to the level it was prior to this meeting. 

The resolution source will be official information from the Reserve Bank of Australia, including the statement or release from its November 2026 meeting, scheduled for November 2-3, 2026, as listed on the official RBA calendar (https://www.rba.gov.au/schedules-events/calendar/?topics=monetary-policy-board). This market may resolve as soon as the statement or release of the Reserve Bank of Australia Monetary Policy Board resulting from its November 2026 meeting with relevant data is issued.

If the specified rate is defined by an upper and lower bound, the relevant change will be the change to the upper bound.

If the specified rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded according to the following guidelines. Increases or decreases of less than 25 bps will be rounded to 25 bps (e.g. an increase or decrease of 10 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 25 bps). Increases or decreases of greater than 25 bps will be rounded to the nearest 25 bps and will be rounded away from 0 in cases of equidistance (e.g., an increase or decrease of 37.5 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 50 bps). Displayed options of "Increase" or "Decrease" will include policy rate increases or decreases of any size.

If the specified meeting is postponed to a date and time before the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve based on the outcome of that postponed meeting.

If the specified meeting is cancelled, or postponed such that no decision is announced by the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No Change" bracket. Emergency changes to the specified rate not resulting from the specified meeting will not be considered.

This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

questions.detail: YES if NVIDIA announces, between 2026-10-03 and 2027-01-31 inclusive, at least one desktop GeForce RTX 50-series card with 'SUPER' in its name, together with a US price or MSRP. The announcement must be made via the NVIDIA Newsroom, NVIDIA GeForce News, or an official NVIDIA keynote backed by such a post. Leaks, partner listings, retailer listings and media reports do not count. Otherwise NO.

forecasts.rationale: Reporting through Jul-Aug 2026 (TrendForce, Benchlife via TweakTown) converges on a CES 2027 (early January) announcement, which falls inside the window, and NVIDIA's GeForce News launch posts normally carry US MSRPs (as with the RTX 40 SUPER at CES 2024). However, the refresh has already slipped repeatedly (CES 2026, then Q2, then Q3, then 'indefinitely'). The blocker, 3GB GDDR7 at $60-70 per module diverted to AI parts, persists, and as of mid-September NVIDIA has not acknowledged the cards exist. Confidence: low; this hinges on one event (CES 2027) and on unresolved memory-supply economics.

questions.title: Will NVIDIA officially announce at least one GeForce RTX 50 'SUPER' desktop graphics card with a US price between 2026-10-03 and 2027-01-31?

questions.detail: YES if, between 2026-10-03 and 2027-03-31, NVIDIA states a US MSRP or 'starting at' price above the launch MSRP for any existing RTX 50 desktop card. Launch MSRPs: 5090 $1,999; 5080 $999; 5070 Ti $749; 5070 $549; 5060 Ti 16 GB $429; 5060 Ti 8 GB $379; 5060 $299; 5050 $249. Qualifying channels: the NVIDIA Newsroom, NVIDIA GeForce News, an NVIDIA US product page, or an NVIDIA statement quoted by Reuters or Bloomberg. Increases only to partner 'kit' prices, retail or marketplace listings, or prices outside the US do not count. Otherwise NO.

forecasts.rationale: NVIDIA has raised partner GPU-kit prices three times in 2026 (Jan, May, ~20-30% later) because of GDDR7 costs, yet it has kept official US MSRPs unchanged. It even sold Founders Editions at launch MSRP at QuakeCon and PAX West in Aug-Sep 2026, while street prices run far above MSRP (RTX 5090 median about $5,000). NVIDIA appears to prefer letting kit and retail prices absorb costs. The main tail is a formal reset around a SUPER launch or a further memory spike. Confidence: medium-low.

questions.title: Will NVIDIA announce an increase to the official US MSRP of any GeForce RTX 50-series desktop graphics card by 2027-03-31?

questions.detail: YES if an official announcement published in the window raises the US MSRP of at least one of these models above its level on 2026-10-03: PS5 $649.99; Xbox Series X 1 TB $799.99; Switch 2 $499.99. Qualifying channels: the PlayStation Blog, Xbox Wire / news.xbox.com, or Nintendo of America news. Price changes only for bundles, new SKUs, retailers or non-US markets do not count. Otherwise NO.

forecasts.rationale: All three just raised US prices: PS5 to $649.99 (Apr 2 2026), Series X to $799.99 (Aug 1 2026), Switch 2 to $499.99 (Sep 1 2026). The base rate across 2025-26 is about 6-7 US hikes in roughly 18 months across the three firms, with Sony's gap ~8 months and Microsoft's ~3-10 months. AI-driven DRAM/NAND pressure is expected to persist into 2027. Fresh hikes and the US-China tariff truce extension reduce near-term pressure, but a 9-month window across three makers keeps this near even. Confidence: low-medium.
